page: Amazon Web Services r6a.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processors operating at up to 3.6 GHz, providing 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 19 Gbps. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, necessitating external network-attached storage solutions.

Benchmark results highlight strong computational and cryptographic capability. In synthetic CPU testing, the instance achieved top-tier ratings with a stress-ng multi-core score of 71,805.19 and a PassMark CPU score of 54,507.49, accompanied by strong PassMark encryption throughput at 56,930.71. Geekbench multi-core performance measured 14,544.0, with strong showings in ray tracing and image processing. Memory throughput exhibits 66.98 GB/sec uncached read and 31.99 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth, landing in the middle 50% tier alongside an average Redis SET performance of 50.51 million operations per second.

The 1:8 core-to-memory balance delivers high resource density for enterprise workloads requiring extensive in-memory footprint relative to CPU overhead. However, the absence of local NVMe storage and AVX-512 instruction support presents explicit architectural tradeoffs, requiring dependence on external storage networks and standard AVX vector execution. In LLM benchmarks, the instance yields 274.72 tokens per second for small-model generation, declining to 16.24 tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

Amazon Web Services r6a.12xlarge is configured for large memory-resident workloads, including distributed in-memory caches, enterprise relational databases, medium-scale machine learning inference, and broad enterprise memory-intensive applications.
